title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZP (Strike off name of Producer Company)

content.overview: Section 378ZP provides for striking off a Producer Company's name in specified circumstances, including failure to commence business within one year of registration, cessation of business with Members, or the Registrar's satisfaction after inquiry that the company no longer carries on its section 378B objects. It includes a show-cause notice and reasonable opportunity to represent the case, a separate route under section 248 for failure to maintain mutual assistance principles, and a Tribunal appeal within sixty days for a Member aggrieved by an order under subsection (1). An appeal under subsection (3) suspends the effect of the strike-off order until the appeal is disposed of.
content.glance: Section 378ZP sets specified strike-off grounds, notice and representation safeguards, a section 248 route, and a sixty-day Tribunal appeal for a Member aggrieved by an order under subsection (1).
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZP (Strike off name of Producer Company). The section identifies circumstances in which the Registrar shall order strike-off, including failure to commence business within one year of registration, cessation of business with Members, or a finding after inquiry that the company no longer carries on any object specified in section 378B. Before an order under subsection (1), the Registrar must give a show-cause notice to the Producer Company, copy it to all directors, and allow a reasonable opportunity to represent the case. Subsection (2) refers to section 248 where the Registrar has reasonable cause to believe mutual assistance principles are not maintained. A Member aggrieved by an order under subsection (1) may appeal to the Tribunal within sixty days; the order does not take effect until that appeal is disposed of. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Grounds under subsection (1)
sections.body: The Registrar shall make an order striking off the company's name where it fails to commence business within one year of registration, ceases to transact business with Members, or the Registrar is satisfied after inquiry that it no longer carries on any object specified in section 378B.

sections.heading: Notice and opportunity
sections.body: No order under subsection (1) may be passed until a show-cause notice of the proposed action has been given to the Producer Company, with a copy to all directors, and a reasonable opportunity to represent its case has been provided.

sections.heading: Mutual assistance principles
sections.body: Where the Registrar has reasonable cause to believe that the Producer Company is not maintaining the mutual assistance principles specified in the section, subsection (2) directs strike-off in accordance with section 248.

sections.heading: Appeal and effect of order
sections.body: A Member aggrieved by an order under subsection (1) may appeal to the Tribunal within sixty days. If such an appeal is filed, the strike-off order does not take effect until the appeal is disposed of.

examples.title: Reviewing a proposed strike-off
examples.body: Identify the statutory ground relied on, verify the inquiry where relevant, check the show-cause notice and opportunity to represent, and determine whether a Member has filed an appeal within the statutory period before treating an order under subsection (1) as effective.

hypotheticals.question: The Registrar proposes to strike off a Producer Company's name, and a Member challenges the order. What section 378ZP safeguards are relevant?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the ground for strike-off and whether the notice, copy to directors and reasonable opportunity to represent were provided. If an order under subsection (1) was made, check whether an aggrieved Member appealed to the Tribunal within sixty days; a filed appeal prevents the order from taking effect until disposal. Do not conflate this route with the subsection (2) reference to section 248.

misconceptions.correction: Identify which subsection and ground apply to the facts.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the show-cause notice and reasonable opportunity required before an order under subsection (1).
misconceptions.correction: Check the notice, copy to directors and opportunity to represent before concluding that the subsection (1) process was followed.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming an order under subsection (1) takes effect immediately even when a Member has appealed within the statutory route.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (4) says the order does not take effect until the appeal is disposed of when an appeal under subsection (3) is filed.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zp do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The Registrar may strike the name of a Producer Company off the register where the company is not carrying on business or is not in operation, after the notice the section requires.
